chunks: And from him, from Ibrahim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him):

Regarding a Magian woman who embraced Islam before her husband had sexual intercourse with her, and her husband refused to embrace Islam, Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that she is entitled to half of the dowry, and he said: 'Islam has not increased her except in honor.'

key_terms.أَنْ يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: Before sexual intercourse/consummation of the marriage.
key_terms.الصَّدَاقِ: The dowry (mahr) given to the wife.
key_terms.مَجُوسِيَّةٍ: A female follower of Magianism (Zoroastrianism), a People of the Book in Shia jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What is the dowry ruling for a woman who converts to Islam before consummation if her husband does not convert?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that a woman who converts to Islam before consummation with her non-Muslim husband is entitled to half the dowry, establishing a precedent for financial equity in mixed-faith divorces. The phrase 'Islam did not add to her except honor' underscores the theological principle that conversion elevates a woman's spiritual and legal standing, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of marriage with People of the Book or Magians.
